description: A dedicated team of space enthusiasts, developers, and problem solvers united for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Irbid. Our mission is to turn complex Martian terrain and environmental data into practical, life-saving insights that empower humanity's next giant leap on the Red Planet
summary: Navigating Mars presents extreme terrain hazards and overwhelming raw data, putting future explorers at risk. Our solution is an interactive web guide for Jezero Crater that transforms complex planetary data into actionable survival insights, combining multi-layered maps with real-time AI assistance and an emergency SOS system.
details:
Our project is an interactive, web-based mapping application designed specifically for Jezero Crater on Mars. The system brings together multi-layered elevation maps, topographical views, images, and scientific data points, including the locations of rock samples collected by the Perseverance rover.

How It Works & Key Features:

Interactive Mapping & Layers: Users can explore the crater's terrain dynamically, switching between topographical and elevation layers to examine specific sites of interest.

AI Exploration Assistant: An integrated AI assistant helps users and researchers analyze Martian formations, understand geological contexts, and instantly retrieve scientific information by asking questions directly through the interface.

Emergency SOS Hazard System: In critical situations, users can trigger a dedicated emergency button that instantly broadcasts a distress signal, marks the exact coordinates on the Martian map, and prompts the AI to calculate survival protocols and safe evacuation routes.

Impact & Objectives:

The project bridges the gap between complex planetary science and practical survival navigation, offering an intuitive tool that enhances safety, supports mission planning, and makes exploring Martian terrain accessible and efficient.
